Personal Account

An account shared by Mr. Hsu, a fellow practitioner, reborn through the help of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

[Testimony of Rebirth] From Exhausted Blessings to Renewed Vows: My Three Years of Being Rescued by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

1. A lost past: on the edge of exhausted blessings

There was a time when I was deeply lost without even knowing it. In those days I did many wrong things that I am ashamed to recall today:

Not honoring my parents: ignoring their kindness, growing arrogant. Stealing as a child: greedy for my own desires, planting the causes of poverty and unease. Promiscuity: harming my reputation and the vital energy of body and mind. Hurting others with harsh words: speaking wildly and creating countless bad connections.

In that state of constantly doing wrong, I could feel my "blessings" running out. At twenty I clearly sensed the breath of death. My body was in great pain, a suffering for which the doctors could find no cause. The dryness deep in my soul made me understand: if I did not turn back, my life would soon come to an end.

2. Turning point and vow: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's rescue

At my most desperate, when I could hardly hold on, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva compassionately did not give up on me. Through the Ksitigarbha Sutra, which accords with the conditions of the world, I made a sincere vow.

This vow changed the course of my life: Leading group practice: the Bodhisattva arranged for me to lead others in reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra.

Speaking of causes and conditions: from a person of harsh speech, I became one who explains cause and effect to others and shares the wisdom of the Dharma.

Practicing altruism: the Bodhisattva opened countless opportunities for me to help beings, so that in giving I could mend the cracks of my past.

3. Adverse conditions that aid growth: two perspectives, worldly and Dharma

After beginning to study Buddhism, many people assume everything will go smoothly from then on. But I must honestly tell everyone that these three years have been extremely hard. Seen by "worldly standards", I seem to have become very "unlucky":

injuries to my body, losing money, being blamed and scolded every day. But seen through the Dharma, this is exactly what is called "adverse conditions that aid growth".

These hardships help me dissolve the heavy wrongs of my past. Without these setbacks, the gate of bodhi wisdom in my heart could not open. Every injury and every humiliation has been tempering my character, letting me realize how deep causes and conditions run.

4. Miracles and faith: real transformation

Although outer circumstances are hard, two very real miracles have happened to me, making my faith in the Dharma unshakable:

A miracle of body and mind: from feeling at twenty that I was about to die, to now at twenty-three — since I began reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra I have not been ill again, and the pain whose cause could never be found has vanished like smoke.

Safety for my family: in the past disasters at home never stopped; now even when big things happen, danger turns to safety and big troubles become small.

5. Words for beginners

I want to tell every friend who has just encountered the Dharma: do not fear karma coming to the surface; fear only that your vow is not strong enough.

When you begin to practice, life may not become perfect right away, and you may even face trials. But please remember: that is "clearing out the rubbish", making room in your life to hold wisdom.

I was once lost and burdened with heavy wrongs, and still Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva pulled me up. If you too feel lost or in pain right now, please give yourself a chance and step into the world of the Ksitigarbha Sutra.
